newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLAND CALL UP BUTT FOR MEXICO GAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLAND CALL UP BUTT FOR MEXICO GAME.

text.p: Manchester United forward Nicky Butt received his first England call on Thursday as manager Glenn Hoddle announced a much-changed squad for a home friendly against Mexico on March 29.
Butt, who has helped United to the European Cup semifinals, was one of seven new faces in the 25-man party since last month's 1-0 defeat by Italy at Wembley.
His United team mate Gary Pallister was recalled, along with Martin Keown, Darren Anderton, Jamie Redknapp, Teddy Sheringham and goalkeeper Nigel Martyn.
"I feel the time is right to bring Butt in and have a look at him, have a look at his temperament. I've already seen his talent and he's certainly a player for the future," Hoddle said.
Hoddle said he had not spoken to Manchester United's manager Alex Ferguson about a possible conflict of interests between club and country.
United could be playing in the European Cup final in Munich on May 28, just three days before England face Poland in a vital World Cup qualifier.
"It's not somthing that will be talked about until it becomes relatity," Hoddle said. "Alex and I have got enough on our plates at the moment.
"If the problem is there it would be a nice problem to have and I would converse with Alex."
As well as Butt, three other United players Garry Neville, David Beckham, Gary Pallister could be involved in the same situation.
Alan Shearer is sidelined for the Mexico match following a groin operation and his Newcastle strike partner Les Ferdinand is recovering from a hamstring injury.
Midfielder Paul Merson, who played against Italy, is out following a hernia operation as is his Arsenal team mate and goalkeeper David Seaman who is recovering from a knee operation.

Paul Gascoigne is still out with an ankle injury and Hoddle has remained loyal to Southampton midfielder Matt Le Tissier, the English media's scapegoat after last month's 1-0 home defeat by Italy in a World Cup qualifier.
Hoddle has hinted he might experiment with his side against the Mexicans.
England's next competitive match is a group two World Cup qualifier at home to Georgia on April 30.
Mexico are top of their World Cup qualifying final round group after two matches in which they beat Canada 4-0 and drew 0-0 with Costa Rica.
Squad:
Goalkeepers - Ian Walker (Tottenham Hotspur), David James (Liverpool), Tim Flowers (Blackburn), Nigel Martyn (Leeds)

Defenders - Gary Neville (Manchester United), Graeme Le Saux (Blackburn), Gareth Southgate (Aston Villa), Tony Adams (Arsenal), Sol Campbell (Tottenham Hotspur), Dominic Matteo (Liverpool), Gary Pallister (Manchester United), Martin Keown (Arsenal)

Midfielders - Paul Ince (Inter Milan), David Beckham (Manchester United), Steve McManaman (Liverpool), David Batty (Newcastle), Matthew Le Tissier (Southampton), Robert Lee (Newcastle), Darren Anderton (Tottenham), Jamie Redknapp (Liverpool)
Strikers - Nicky Barmby (Everton), Robbie Fowler (Liverpool), Ian Wright (Arsenal), Nicky Butt (Manchester United), Teddy Sheringham (Tottenham).
